entries.reason: `IF TTL-SECONDS NUMERIC` (704) is false only when the UNSTRING (699-702) puts a non-digit into `TTL-SECONDS` (PIC 9(06), USAGE DISPLAY), e.g. the query `ttl=abc`. The piece is an alphanumeric sender of a numeric MOVE: GnuCOBOL stores `000000`, so NUMERIC is true and 704:false is never taken; on z/OS the non-digit bytes stay and NUMERIC would be false. IBM documents no result for non-digit data in a numeric DISPLAY item (Enterprise COBOL 6.4 Programming Guide SC27-8714-03, ZONEDATA(PFD) assumes valid data; register C11), so the outcome is undefined by IBM, not infeasible: an input does reach it. Scenario `post-ttl-nonnumeric` proves cobc's bytes, not z/OS's. Owner ruling 2026-10-31 (#6839 row J) extends family U from out-of-range subscripts and reference modifications (2026-10-29) to non-digit data in a numeric DISPLAY item.

`IF ETTL-RESP EQUAL DFHRESP(NORMAL) OR ETTL-STATUS EQUAL DFHVALUE(ENABLED)` (718) in 1310-TTL sits inside `IF ZF-TTL GREATER THAN SEVEN-DAYS` (716, 604800 s). ZF-TTL exceeds seven days only if it also exceeds twenty-four hours (86400 s), and then the test at 712-715 ran first: when ETTL-RESP is not NORMAL (or ETTL-STATUS is DISABLED) it MOVEs TWENTY-FOUR-HOURS to ZF-TTL, so 716 is false. Line 718 is therefore reached only with ETTL-RESP NORMAL, and its first operand ETTL-RESP EQUAL NORMAL is then true; no input makes both operands false.
